title: Longest Valid Parentheses
prompt: Given a string `s` containing just the characters `(` and `)`, return the length of the longest valid (well-formed) parentheses substring.

examples.explanation: The longest valid parentheses substring is "()".
The longest valid parentheses substring is "()()".

hints: Only a ')' can ever complete or extend a valid run, so think of dp[i] as: the length of the longest valid substring ENDING exactly at index i (only meaningful when s[i] == ')').
If s[i] == ')' and s[i-1] == '(', they form a fresh pair, extending whatever valid substring ended right before that pair: dp[i] = dp[i-2] + 2.

If s[i] == ')' and s[i-1] == ')', check whether the character just before the matching valid run that ends at i-1 is a '(': if s[i - dp[i-1] - 1] == '(', this new ')' closes over that whole run, so dp[i] = dp[i-1] + 2 + dp[i - dp[i-1] - 2] (the last term folds in anything valid immediately before that matched block).

solution.approach: Define dp[i] as the length of the longest valid parentheses substring ending exactly at index i (0 whenever s[i] is '(' since a valid substring can't end on an open paren). Two cases when s[i] == ')': if s[i-1] == '(', it directly closes a fresh pair, extending whatever was valid before it, dp[i] = dp[i-2] + 2 (or 2 if i < 2). If s[i-1] == ')', it might close over an entire valid run ending at i-1: check the character immediately before that run, at index i - dp[i-1] - 1; if it's '(', this ')' matches it, so dp[i] = dp[i-1] + 2 plus any valid run immediately preceding that opening bracket (dp[i - dp[i-1] - 2], guarded against negative indices). Track the maximum dp value seen as the answer.
